items.prompt: Which word does NOT belong? dog, cat, rabbit, carrot
items.answer: Carrot does not belong. Dog, cat, and rabbit are all animals; carrot is a vegetable.

steps: Carrot — a vegetable, not an animal.

items.prompt: Which word does NOT belong? happy, joyful, glad, angry
items.answer: Angry does not belong. Happy, joyful, and glad all mean feeling pleased or cheerful; angry means feeling mad.

steps: Happy, joyful, glad — all mean feeling good or pleased.
Angry — means feeling mad, not pleased.

items.prompt: Sort these words into two groups — FRUITS and VEGETABLES: apple, carrot, mango, broccoli, banana, spinach.
items.answer: Fruits: apple, mango, banana. Vegetables: carrot, broccoli, spinach.

steps: Fruits (sweet, from flowering plants): apple, mango, banana.
Vegetables (roots, leaves, stems): carrot, broccoli, spinach.

items.prompt: Which word does NOT belong? red, blue, green, circle
items.answer: Circle does not belong. Red, blue, and green are colors; circle is a shape.

steps: Circle — a shape, not a color.

items.prompt: Which pair of words names things that are BOTH animals? (A) rose and eagle  (B) eagle and dolphin  (C) dolphin and daisy
items.answer: B — eagle and dolphin. Both are animals.

steps: Dolphin — a mammal that lives in water (animal).
Rose and daisy are plants, not animals.

items.prompt: Which word describes something that is MORE cold — chilly or freezing?
items.answer: Freezing is more cold. Chilly means a little cold; freezing means extremely cold.

steps: Chilly = slightly cold, like a cool autumn day.
Freezing = very extremely cold, like ice.
Freezing is the more intense word.

items.prompt: Which word describes something that is MORE loud — loud or deafening?
items.answer: Deafening is more loud. Loud means making a lot of noise; deafening means so loud it hurts your ears.

steps: Loud = making a lot of noise.
Deafening = so extremely loud it is painful.

items.prompt: Sort these words into two groups — THINGS IN THE SKY and THINGS IN THE OCEAN: cloud, whale, star, jellyfish, airplane, coral.
items.answer: Things in the sky: cloud, star, airplane. Things in the ocean: whale, jellyfish, coral.

steps: Sky things: cloud (made of water vapor up high), star (in outer space/sky), airplane (flies through the sky).
Ocean things: whale (marine mammal), jellyfish (sea creature), coral (reef organism).

items.prompt: Which word does NOT belong? whisper, murmur, shout, mumble
items.answer: Shout does not belong. Whisper, murmur, and mumble are all quiet ways of speaking; shout means speaking very loudly.

steps: Whisper, murmur, mumble — all quiet or soft speech.

items.prompt: Which word is MORE intense? sad or devastated?
items.answer: Devastated is more intense. Sad means feeling unhappy; devastated means feeling extremely crushed and heartbroken.

steps: Devastated is the stronger, more extreme feeling.

items.prompt: Which word does NOT belong? piano, guitar, drum, pencil
items.answer: Pencil does not belong. Piano, guitar, and drum are all musical instruments; a pencil is a writing tool.

steps: Piano, guitar, drum — all musical instruments.
Pencil — a writing tool, not a musical instrument.

items.prompt: Which word describes something BIGGER — large or enormous?
items.answer: Enormous describes something bigger. Large means a good-sized object; enormous means very, very large.

items.prompt: Sort these words into two groups — THINGS THAT FLY and THINGS THAT SWIM: eagle, trout, butterfly, shark, pelican, dolphin.
items.answer: Things that fly: eagle, butterfly, pelican. Things that swim: trout, shark, dolphin.

items.prompt: Which word is MORE forceful — toss or hurl?
items.answer: Hurl is more forceful. Toss means a light, easy throw; hurl means throwing with great force.

items.prompt: Which word does NOT belong? oak, pine, maple, tulip
items.answer: Tulip does not belong. Oak, pine, and maple are all trees; tulip is a flower.

steps: Tulip — a flower, not a tree.
